summary: The client side of HTTP is covered by URLSession in the SDK, which streams and caches responses, and by the shell's rustls HTTP/1.1 client. The Apple CFHost, CFNetService (Bonjour), proxy, diagnostics, FTP and raw stream APIs have no app-facing counterpart. Network state and DHCP are owned by the system network service, which apps cannot query through an SDK API.

features.note: URLRequest carries URL, method, body and headers. There is no raw serialized HTTP message, no response status line access and no CFHTTPMessageAppendBytes equivalent.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/url.rs (URLSession::bytes, 301/302/303/307/308 followed up to 5 hops); springboard/src/deildu/http.rs (keep-alive, redirects)
features.note: Streaming and redirects work. Persistent connections are reused, but no HTTP/2, no stream properties and no final-URL property are exposed.

features.apple: Cookie storage through CFNetwork and the HTTP stream session (CFHTTPMessage headers; Apple doc mentions no separate cookie API in this framework)
features.note: Wave 3 (w3-cfnetwork, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The SDK URLSession keeps no cookies. Only the Deildu client keeps its own jar; apps get none.

Wave 3 (w3-cfnetwork, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No credentials type and no challenge handling for apps. Decided in docs/bifrost-ui.md section URLSession as a gap (no URLCredential).

features.bifrost: springboard/src/deildu/http.rs (uses a UDP resolver, type Resolver from the dns module, internal only)
features.note: The resolver exists inside the shell's HTTP client. Apps have no name lookup API.

Wave 2 (theme-06, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No proxy settings are read or applied. The Network settings page shows Ethernet, Wi-Fi and a Network Manager row only.
No service discovery or registration API for apps. The shell has no mDNS browser exposed in the SDK.

features.feature: Network configuration, link state and DHCP
features.apple: Network configuration and reachability through SystemConfiguration and CFHostGetReachability (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/cfnetwork/hosts)
features.bifrost: springboard/netd (Wi-Fi, DHCP, routes behind a socket); springboard/src/net/wifi.rs (Status, sysfs link state); springboard/src/net/ntp.rs (online() check); springboard/proto/src/svc.rs (is.olibuijr.net service protocol)
features.note: The system owns Wi-Fi, DHCP and connectivity state and uses it for NTP and the Wi-Fi widget. Apps get no reachability API in the SDK.
The PC has no cellular interface. Service type hints have no counterpart on Linux, and no SDK API exposes them.

features.bifrost: springboard/src/deildu/http.rs (Tls wraps rustls with the webpki roots)
features.note: TLS certificate validation is on, using the webpki roots, for the HTTP client. No per-stream SSL settings, no client identities and no SOCKS.
No diagnostic window or API. The Wi-Fi page shows link state only.

features.bifrost: none found in springboard/sdk/src/url.rs (HTTP and https only)
features.note: FTP is not implemented in the SDK. Low priority for a desktop with a file portal.
Errors are returned as Rust results with the transport message. There is no CFNetworkErrors code mapping.

gaps: No cookie storage or URLCredential/HTTP authentication for URLSession apps (springboard/sdk/src/url.rs)
No host name lookup API for apps (CFHost); the resolver stays inside springboard/src/deildu/http.rs
No proxy configuration read or applied (CFNetworkCopySystemProxySettings)
No Bonjour or network service browse and register API (CFNetService)
No app-facing reachability or connectivity API; springboard/src/net/ntp.rs and springboard/src/net/wifi.rs use it internally only
No network diagnostics window or API (CFNetDiagnostic)
No raw HTTP message API (CFHTTPMessage) and no HTTP/2
